headline: US equity futures point lower as Brent holds above $90 on US–Iran tensions and rising yields ahead of a jobs-heavy week
raw_text:
- S&P 500 (@ES), Dow Jones (@YM), Nasdaq 100 (@NQ) and Russell 2000 (@ER2) futures are set to open lower by about 0.37–0.40% as of 9:05 AM ET amid higher oil prices and bond yields
- Brent crude (@QA) trades around $91 per barrel, up over 3% overnight, after renewed U.S.-Iran military strikes in the Strait of Hormuz spark inflation and supply-disruption fears
- Valero Energy (VLO) rises 2.23%, Phillips 66 (PSX) gains 2.16% and Chevron (CVX) trades higher pre-market as energy names lead on the oil spike
- PayPal (PYPL) falls roughly 1% pre-market after disappointing results reported on Friday
- Shein shares drop at least 10% in Hong Kong pre-debut gray-market trading ahead of its downsized Hong Kong IPO listing
- SAIC (SAIC) and BLRX (BLRX) report earnings before the bell, with SAIC (SAIC)’s Q2 results due and a conference call scheduled for 10 AM ET
- A light U.S. macro calendar today features the Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index at 9:30 AM ET and Treasury bill auctions at 10:30 AM ET
- Asian markets trade mixed to lower, with Japan’s Nikkei (@NKD) off 0.1% to 0.4% and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng down 0.4%, while European bourses trade cautiously to softer amid thin UK holiday volumes and rising yields
- Higher bond yields and increased odds of delayed Fed rate cuts set the backdrop for a week that includes the Fed’s Beige Book and key U.S. jobs data
